    feat(product-view): add renderHeader slot for caller-supplied header content
    
    Adds one optional prop to ProductView so a caller can supply the header block, and
    corrects two documentation claims in the same file that were false or misleading.
    
    The slot
    ---------
    renderHeader?: (props: ProductViewHeaderProps) => React.ReactNode
    
    Its default renders the same private ProductViewHeader the base file renders inline, with
    the identical six values, so omitting it is behaviour-preserving. Both header call sites
    route through it — base renders the header twice behind responsive display arrays, and a
    slot only one of them honoured would be a silent half-override.
    
    Prop, default and call sites are one atomic unit, not three separable edits: deleting the
    default alone produces TS2722 at both call sites.
    
    Why the default export rather than a named-export wrapper
    ----------------------------------------------------------
    overrideStyling.md prescribes putting Zimmermann-only additions behind a named export that
    wraps the default. That route cannot express this requirement: a wrapper can only set props
    the default already accepts, so letting a caller replace an internal render block still
    requires the slot on the default. The only alternative is forking the component body, which
    is a graver breach of the faithful-port rule.
    
    The rule's stated purpose is served. renderHeader has zero occurrences in the base package,
    and the four base modules that import product-view — product-view-modal/index.jsx,
    product-view-modal/bundle.jsx, bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx and
    pages/product-detail/index.jsx — neither pass it nor are affected by it. forwardRef
    behaviour is unchanged.
    
    Note overrideStyling.md cites product-tile/index.tsx (CardBaseline) and link/index.tsx as
    established precedent for the named-export split. Neither exists in overrides/, and
    CardBaseline appears nowhere in the codebase. Raised separately.
    
    Documentation corrections
    --------------------------
    The header's list of differences from base was exhaustive and became false the moment the
    prop landed; it is now scoped to name the addition.
    
    ProductViewRefScope's JSDoc told consumers to assert Ref<T> at the prop site. That is not
    required — TypeScript accepts the this-typed callback as a ref unaided, verified by removing
    the equivalent assertion and observing a clean typecheck against a live probe. The guidance
    sat in a shared component, so it propagated. It is now descriptive.
    
    Three inert casts removed
    --------------------------
    The cloneElement trio narrowed nothing: customButton.props is any, since React.ReactElement
    defaults P = any, and Partial<unknown> is {}. typescript.md reserves `as` for genuinely
    overriding inference, so documenting them would not have cured them. Removed with the
    comment that existed only to explain them; that block is now byte-identical to base
    index.jsx:493-503 modulo house formatting.

    re-checked after the line shift.
